title: てある, ている and ておく
summary: ている shows a thing in a state, てある shows a state left by someone's action, and ておく sets an action up and leaves its effect in place.

blocks.text: Textbooks give you English labels for these helpers. This lesson asks what each one really does. All three sit after the **て-form** of a verb, and the choice between them depends on one thing: **who or what is behind the action**.
ている with a self-move verb

A **self-move** verb (lesson 15) such as 開く describes something that happens to the subject by itself. With ている it simply describes a **state**: the window is in the open state. Nobody is mentioned. Japanese treats the window as if it were a little living thing that is "being" open.
店が開いている。 The shop is open.
てある with an other-move verb

An **other-move** verb such as 開ける needs someone to do it. With **ある** the window loses its "alive" feel: it is just a thing that someone acted on, and the result is still there. The marked noun (the window) stays the main carriage with **が**, but a hidden person caused the state.
窓が開けてある。 The window has been opened (by someone).

blocks.jp: 黒板に名前が書いてある。
blocks.en: A name has been written on the board (and it is there).

blocks.jp: 机の上に本が置いてある。
blocks.en: A book has been put on the desk (and sits there).

blocks.jp: 冷蔵庫にケーキが入れてある。
blocks.en: Someone has put a cake in the fridge.

blocks.text: This is also why Japanese says 「と書いてある」 for writing on an object: the words were put there by someone, and they stay.
ておく: do it and leave it in place

ておく is the active side of てある. The verb **おく** means "to place", so you carry out the action and **leave its effect in place**. Look at the particle: てある keeps 窓**が** (the window is the main carriage), but ておく has 窓**を** (the person acts on it). It is two sides of one coin: 窓が開けてある (the window's view) and 窓を開けておく (the doer's view).
窓を開けておく。 I open the window and leave it.

blocks.jp: 旅行の前に切符を買っておく。
blocks.en: I buy the ticket before the trip and have it ready.

blocks.text: Textbooks say "do in advance", and that is often true, but a future purpose is not required: you can put an empty jar into a cupboard just to get it out of the way, or shut something away and leave it locked up.

blocks.jp: 空のびんを戸棚に置いておいた。
blocks.en: I put the empty jar in the cupboard and left it there.
I let the child go on crying (and leave it that way). 泣かせる is the causative from lesson 19.

blocks.text: Here are the three together. Only the verb and the ending change.

rows: The window is open (just the state)
The window is open because someone opened it
Open the window and leave it that way

items: **Self-move verb (自動詞) + ている**: a state, no one behind it.
**Other-move verb (他動詞) + てある**: a state someone left behind.
**て-form + おく**: do it and leave the effect in place.
Never use ある after a self-move verb: 開いてある is wrong.

questions.note: ておく: do it and leave the result ready.
questions.en: Please buy drinks before the party.

questions.instruction: What does this say?
options: The door is opening by itself
Someone opened the door and it is still open
questions.note: Other-move verb + てある: a state left by someone.
questions.en: The door has been left open.

questions.instruction: Which sentence is wrong?
questions.note: Never use ある after a self-move verb.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.note: かける is other-move; someone hung the picture.
questions.en: A picture has been hung on the wall.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap (the state of a self-move verb)
questions.note: つく is self-move, so ている.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap (leave it that way)
questions.prompt: 電気を＿＿おいてください。
questions.note: て-form + おく after an other-move verb.

questions.prompt: ノートに名前が書いてある。
options: A name is being written now
Someone wrote a name and it is there
questions.note: Other-move verb + てある: the written name stays.
questions.en: A name is written in the notebook.

questions.note: Self-move + ている: a plain state.

questions.instruction: True or false: this sentence is correct
questions.note: 開く is self-move: the state is 開いている.

questions.instruction: True or false?
questions.prompt: ておく always means doing something in advance for the future.
questions.note: You can also leave an effect in place for no future purpose.

questions.instruction: Which verb is other-move (the kind てある needs)?
questions.note: 閉める needs someone to do it (other-move); 閉まる closes by itself.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says "Someone has left the light on"?
questions.note: Other-move verb つける + てある.

questions.instruction: What does the verb おく mean on its own?
questions.note: ておく: do it and place the result.

questions.instruction: Which sentence keeps が for the window?
questions.note: てある keeps が; ておく takes を.
